tasks.title: Closing-review fixes: grader flag, preflight branches, env fields, changelog
tasks.summary: Factory-level. `bs results check --as grader` accepts the shared `--artifacts-dir` and says it is inert there, and the grader template says why; intake problems name their input, with the judges label split; wave.md step 7 maps every preflight result to one of five branches, so a worker-file problem is a counted `gate run` round or a logged return bounded at one that obeys the ladder; queue-and-gate.md names the per-check `environment` field; the changelog says what the release does.
tasks.objective: Factory-level fix for four of the five closing-review findings on plan v4 (spec review bs-gate-bounce-run-2026-10-29#143, integration head 6365aca3), as revised by two pre-code reviews of the v5 draft (round 1: findings f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-f945754b, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-81ee8bc6, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-0fb76701 and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-2381b9b1, bs-gate-bounce-run-2026-10-29#148 to #151; round 2: f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-45a7d16b, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-1ecb562b and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-ca1f180a, #155 to #157; round 3: f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-246f97c8, #161); the fifth closing finding, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-b1e98459, was fixed in the epic spec itself. Line numbers are at that head; the symbol named beside each is the reference if a line has moved. (a) Findings f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-ea78e56c (S2), f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-0fb76701 (S3) and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-2381b9b1 (S4). `bs results check --as grader` refuses `--artifacts-dir` with `cli.flag-not-for-mode`, because `RESULTS_CHECK_FLAGS.grader` (factory/orchestrator/src/cli.ts:1238) is `['as', 'grader', ...SESSION_FLAGS]`, while AC4 as signed off, .claude/agents/bs-grader.md:144 and .claude/skills/bs/wave.md:403 give the grader line the same `--artifacts-dir <work-root>/state/artifacts` as every other line. End state, which keeps AC4 true as signed off: grader mode accepts `--artifacts-dir`. The grader stage reads no artifact (paperwork.ts `STAGES_FOR_ROLE.grader` is `['grader']`), so the flag only sets the `artifact_home` the output reports, which `runResultsCheck` already computes in every mode with `artifactHome(taskId, flags['artifacts-dir'])`. Say so, never silently: when the flag is given under `--as grader`, the output's `warnings` carries one entry that names `--artifacts-dir` and says the grader stage reads no artifact, and `skipped` keeps the `artifacts` stage as `not-checked-for-grader`. The output keeps its top-level keys and its exit codes. Grader mode keeps refusing every flag it refuses today apart from this one (the envelope flags, `--result`, `--worktree`, `--base`, `--plan`, the gate-only flags), and no other mode's flags change. The grader line in bs-grader.md and in wave.md step 8 keeps the flag. Because every sanctioned grader run now prints that warning, bs-grader.md says once, outside its SHARED regions and beside its preflight line, why the line carries the flag (every preflight line in a wave shares one `--artifacts-dir`), that the grader stage reads no artifact, and that the warning about it is expected, is not a problem to fix, and the flag stays (finding 2381b9b1); the grader reads its template, not wave.md, so the sentence goes there. Make every description of the per-mode flags match the code: the `results check` summary in factory/orchestrator/src/usage.ts (the entry at :626, 'each also takes [--agent --provider --model-tier], [--artifacts-dir] and the session flags where it reads them') and docs/guide/operator-guide/queue-and-gate.md:487 ('Each worker mode also takes `--agent --provider --model-tier` and `--artifacts-dir`', and grader mode refuses the envelope flags) say that `--as coder` and `--as tester` take the envelope flags, that all three worker modes take `--artifacts-dir`, and that under `--as grader` it only sets the reported `artifact_home`. Close the test gap the finding names: test/handbackPreflight.test.ts checks each line against the union of every mode's flags (`flagSpecFor('results', 'check')`), so it could not see a refusal in one mode, and no test ran a template's line through the verb. Add a test that runs the concrete preflight lines through the built CLI (`runCli` from test/helpers/cliHarness.ts): the lines whose `--as` is a literal mode, which are bs-coder.md's, bs-tester.md's and bs-grader.md's own lines, wave.md step 7's `--as gate` line and step 8's coder, tester and grader lines, seven in all (finding 0fb76701). The generic `bs results check <task-id> --as <role>` line in the handback-preflight fragment and its SHARED regions is prose and is not run. Each placeholder is filled with a value of its flag's type: an integer for `--plan-version` and for `<round>`, a `model_tier` value from taxonomy.yml for `--model-tier`, a provider name for `--provider`, a role for `--agent`, scratch paths for file and directory flags, and a session id and one of its event ids for `--session` and `--causal-parent`. (b) Findings f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-5f8da50c (S3), f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-f945754b (S2), f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-81ee8bc6 (S3), f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-45a7d16b (S3), f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-1ecb562b (S3) and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-246f97c8 (S3). wave.md step 7, 'The preflight comes first' (wave.md:294-296), says that while the `--as gate` preflight exits 1 the wave-runner 'fixes its own flags or bounces the problem to the worker whose file it names, and does not call `gate run`'. A bounce taken there writes no `gate-outcome`, and escalation.ts `readFailedRounds` counts only blocked gate-outcomes, so no rung trips and nothing but the epic token cap ends the loop. Sending every agent-file problem through `gate run` is not enough either: the `gate run` branch of cli.ts reads and stamps the result (`readJsonFile`, `stampResultEnvelope`), mints the evidence and uiux-visual files (`mintFromEvidence`, `mintFromUiuxVisual`), closes the handed-in judge turns (`recordJudgeReport`) and reads the grader file before it calls `runGate`, and each of those throws on a bad file, so such a problem writes no `gate-outcome` and cannot be counted that way. Code change, so that each problem maps to one branch from fields the output carries: every `intake` problem `runResultsCheck` prints carries `input`, which names where it came from. That is a flag's file or value (`result`, `grader`, `checks`, `findings`, `evidence`, `uiux-visual`, `lessons`, `plan`), the task id and artifacts dir (`artifacts`), or a step inside the verb (`judge-dispatch`, `judge-artifact`, `judge-internal`, `paperwork`). The verb's single `judges` label is split, because it covered the wave-runner's own judge bookkeeping, a judge's file and the log read at once (finding 1ecb562b): a judge close that fails with a `judges.*` code starting `judges.artifact-` (the judge's file is missing, stale, unparseable or not a list) is `judge-artifact`; one that fails with any other `judges.*` code (no dispatch recorded for that role or round, a kind the role may not report, no declared artifact) is `judge-dispatch`; a failure reading the session's judge turns, or a close error that is not a `judges.*` code, is `judge-internal`. `paperwork` stays the label of an exception inside `checkPaperwork`. End state in wave.md step 7, with the ladder, its count and escalation.ts unchanged: before reading problems the wave-runner makes its line match step 7's example flag for flag (the envelope flags included, each file the one the steps name); an `error` document or a difference is its own line. Then every problem falls in exactly one of five branches. (1) The wave-runner's own: `deps-missing` (the install of the worktree it set up) and an `intake` problem whose `input` is `artifacts`, `checks`, `findings`, `lessons`, `plan` or `judge-dispatch`. It fixes that (for `judge-dispatch`, its own judge records or line) and runs the preflight again; no agent runs again, so this is not a round. (2) A judge turn that is not in order: `judges-outstanding`, `uiux-spec-missing`, `uiux-visual-missing`, and an `intake` problem whose `input` is `grader`, `evidence`, `uiux-visual` or `judge-artifact`. It takes, re-pokes or re-runs that judge turn under the existing rules of steps 5 to 7, unchanged; a judge's turn is not a ladder round. (3) A worker's file the gate blocks on: `schema-invalid`, `artifacts-missing`, `not-committed`, `screenshots-missing`, `screenshots-stale` and `grader-invalid`. It runs `gate run` with the same flags, which blocks on the same reason before any check command runs and writes the blocked `gate-outcome` that `readFailedRounds` counts; the bounce that follows is step 9's, a failed round on the ladder that `bs escalation check` reads. (4) A worker's result the gate cannot count: an `intake` problem whose `input` is `result`. `gate run` would throw on it before writing any event, so the wave-runner does not run it. It appends one `error-logged` event whose fields carry the facts, not only its `detail`: `task_id` and `task_ref` the task, `agent` and `agent_role` the worker's role, `error` `contract.schema-violation` (the class `GATE_BLOCK_ERROR_CLASSES` gives a missing or malformed file), `severity` `S3-minor`, and `detail` naming the input and the reason. It returns the result to that worker at most once per task, as a builder `dispatch_decision` for that role whose `causal_parent` is that `error-logged` event (and whose `continuation_of` names the worker's earlier dispatch when the same agent is resumed). So the count of returns per task and role is the number of builder dispatches whose causal parent is such an event, readable off the log. A second `result` intake problem on the same task goes to the epic session, which returns it no more without the operator's answer; before the operator, there is one return. (5) The verb or the log failed: an `intake` problem whose `input` is `judge-internal` or `paperwork`, or one whose `input` this list does not name. It goes to the epic session and never to an agent; it is not a round. Precedence, because one preflight result can hold problems from several branches (finding 246f97c8): `runResultsCheck` prints `problems` as every intake problem first, then the stage problems of `checkPaperwork`, which runs whenever the result is usable even after an intake problem, and the top-level `reason` is the first of them; `gate run` reads its files, mints the evidence and uiux-visual files and closes the judge turns before `runGate`, so while any intake problem shows, `gate run` throws and writes no `gate-outcome`. So the wave-runner settles the result in this order and runs the preflight again after each step: first every `intake` problem, by its branch (5 stops the task and goes to the epic session; then 1; then 2; then 4); then the stage reasons of branches 1 and 2; and a stage reason of branch 3 goes to `gate run` only when the preflight shows no `intake` problem. A handed-in grader file that is fresh but neither a list nor a grader document shows both `judge-artifact` (intake, `judges.artifact-not-a-list`) and `grader-invalid` (stage) for the same file; it takes branch 2 and is never sent to `gate run`. Tie-break: a named problem that the line or a worker could have caused (an unreadable result at the path the worker reported) is the worker's, branch 3 if it carries a paperwork stage and branch 4 if `intake`. Every dispatch these branches make for a builder role (escalation.ts `BUILDER_ROLES`: coder, tester, uiux), a branch-4 return or a re-run uiux pass included, is a builder dispatch like any other, and the ladder applies to it unchanged: from the task's second blocked `gate-outcome`, the first builder dispatch after it runs on a strictly higher model tier than the failing round's (`checkModelTierRung`); from the third, no builder dispatch and no gate round goes out before an operator answer (`checkOperatorRung`). The sentence ending 'and does not call `gate run`' goes. queue-and-gate.md section 5 ('Before hand-back: `bs results check`', near :503) documents `input`, states the five branches and the precedence. It names branch 4's bound as a playbook rule: the log evidences it by structure, and no verb enforces it, an accepted gap like the port-0 rule. Pin the premises in code: a branch-3 defect becomes a counted round with no check run, and a branch-4 defect makes `gate run` write no `gate-outcome`. escalation.ts, budgets.yml's `escalation_ladder`, gate.ts, judges.ts and wave.md step 9 stay as they are. (c) Finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-7d2d0eff (S3): queue-and-gate.md 'An env-failure block' (queue-and-gate.md:509-520) says the `testgate-result`, the `gate-outcome` and the blocked outcome carry `environment_evidence` with one entry per check. The code puts every check's entry, in result order, in the `testgate-result` payload's `environment` array (gate.ts, the `testgate-result` emit), and puts `error_class: execution.env-failure` with `environment_evidence` on the `testgate-result` and `gate-outcome` events only when a failed check's own clock gap shows sleep, holding only those checks' entries (gate.ts `sleptFailedChecks` and `finalize`); `gate run`'s printed outcome carries them as `error_class` and `environmentEvidence`, beside `testResult.environment`. Rewrite that paragraph to say exactly this, and list the `CheckEnvironment` fields (testgate.ts: `name`, `window`, `wall_ms`, `monotonic_ms`, `clock_gap_ms`, `load_1m_start`, `load_1m_end`, `cpus`) once, under the field that holds every check. The rest of the section stays: the command-only window, `SLEEP_GAP_MS`, load as evidence only, the lock-wait timeout, the outcome that stays blocked, and the ladder paragraph. (d) Finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-acc5dbee (S4): in CHANGELOG.md `## Unreleased`, the task-6 bullet ends '`gate.ts` is untouched.' (CHANGELOG.md:78), true of that task's diff and false of the release, where tasks 1 and 3 changed the gate. Reword it to say what the release does: the gate writes the events it wrote before, and recurrence reads the class when it counts. Two more sentences in the same section have the same shape and get the same fix: the task-5 bullet's 'No production change.' (CHANGELOG.md:72) and the `### Changed` CLI-tests entry's 'Nothing in the npm package changes.' (CHANGELOG.md:92). Each says instead what its own change touches: the two tests and their fixture; tests and CI. Add one entry for this task to the epic's `### Added` list, written like the others: what the release does. Read, never edit: bs-coder.md, bs-tester.md, .claude/fragments/, every SHARED region in bs-grader.md, .claude/skills/bs/dispatch.md, escalation.ts, gate.ts, testgate.ts, paperwork.ts, test/helpers/ and budgets.yml.
acceptance_criteria: Finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-ea78e56c: `bs results check <task-id> --as grader --grader <file> --artifacts-dir <dir>` is accepted. On a well-formed grader file it exits 0, reports `artifact_home` as the task's home under `<dir>`, keeps the `artifacts` stage in `skipped` as `not-checked-for-grader`, and carries one `warnings` entry that names `--artifacts-dir` and says the grader stage reads no artifact; without the flag no such warning appears. Grader mode still refuses `--agent`, `--result`, `--worktree`, `--base` and `--plan` as `cli.flag-not-for-mode` and every gate-only flag as `cli.gate-only-flag`. test/cliResultsCheck.test.ts pins each through the built CLI, and was seen to fail before the cli.ts change.

Findings f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-ea78e56c and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-0fb76701: test/handbackPreflight.test.ts runs, through the built CLI (`runCli`), exactly the concrete preflight lines, the ones whose `--as` is a literal `coder`, `tester`, `grader` or `gate`: one each in bs-coder.md, bs-tester.md and bs-grader.md, wave.md step 7's `--as gate` line and step 8's three per-role lines. It requires that it found seven, the two grader lines among them, and it never runs the generic `--as <role>` line of the handback-preflight fragment. The lines are read from the files, not copied into the test. Each placeholder is filled with a value of its flag's type: an integer for `--plan-version` and `<round>`, a taxonomy `model_tier` for `--model-tier`, a provider name, a role for `--agent`, scratch paths under a `mkdtemp` directory for files and directories, a session id and one of its event ids for `--session` and `--causal-parent`, with `BS_HOME` pointed at another `mkdtemp` directory; both directories are removed afterwards. Each run prints the paperwork document, with `as` equal to its mode and an `outcome`, never an `error` document; a blocked outcome on scratch input is expected. The existing parse against usage.ts (`expectParses`) stays. `notes` shows the test discriminates: with `'artifacts-dir'` taken out of grader mode in cli.ts it fails on the bs-grader.md line and on the wave.md step-8 grader line, and the output of that run is quoted.

Finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-ea78e56c: the `results check` summary in usage.ts and queue-and-gate.md section 5 state the per-mode flags as the code accepts them: `--as coder` and `--as tester` take `--agent --provider --model-tier`; all three worker modes take `--artifacts-dir`; under `--as grader` it only sets the reported `artifact_home`, because the grader stage reads no artifact. test/handbackPreflight.test.ts pins both texts and fails if either says grader mode takes the envelope flags.

Finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-2381b9b1: bs-grader.md says once, outside its SHARED regions and beside its preflight line, that the line carries `--artifacts-dir` so every preflight line in a wave shares one value, that the grader stage reads no artifact, and that the warning the preflight prints about that flag is expected, is not a problem to fix, and the flag stays. The sentence names no tool, package manager or test runner, and the agent-template neutrality check in `bash scripts/check.sh` passes. The grader's line itself is unchanged. test/handbackPreflight.test.ts pins the sentence outside the SHARED regions, and the existing grader-template assertions hold.

Findings f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-5f8da50c, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-f945754b, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-81ee8bc6, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-45a7d16b, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-1ecb562b and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-246f97c8: wave.md step 7 maps every preflight result to exactly one branch. First the line must match step 7's example flag for flag; an `error` document or a difference is the wave-runner's own line. Then: (1) the wave-runner's own, `deps-missing` and an `intake` problem whose `input` is `artifacts`, `checks`, `findings`, `lessons`, `plan` or `judge-dispatch`: it fixes that and runs the preflight again, which is not a round; (2) a judge turn not in order, `judges-outstanding`, `uiux-spec-missing`, `uiux-visual-missing` and an `intake` problem whose `input` is `grader`, `evidence`, `uiux-visual` or `judge-artifact`: the existing judge rules of steps 5 to 7; (3) a worker's file the gate blocks on, `schema-invalid`, `artifacts-missing`, `not-committed`, `screenshots-missing`, `screenshots-stale` and `grader-invalid`: `gate run` with the same flags, a counted blocked `gate-outcome`, and step 9's bounce; (4) a worker's result the gate cannot count, an `intake` problem whose `input` is `result`: no `gate run`; one `error-logged` whose fields (`task_id`, `task_ref`, `agent`, `agent_role`, `error` `contract.schema-violation`, `severity` `S3-minor`) carry the facts, with `detail` naming the input and reason; at most one return per task, as a builder `dispatch_decision` whose `causal_parent` is that event; a second goes to the epic session, which returns it no more without the operator's answer; (5) the verb or the log, an `intake` problem whose `input` is `judge-internal`, `paperwork` or one the list does not name: the epic session, never an agent. Precedence for a result that holds problems from several branches: the wave-runner settles every `intake` problem first, by its branch (5 first, then 1, 2 and 4), then the stage reasons of branches 1 and 2, re-running the preflight after each; a stage reason goes to `gate run` (branch 3) only when the preflight shows no `intake` problem, because `gate run` throws before `runGate` while one remains. Tie-break: a named problem the line or a worker could have caused is the worker's (branch 3 or 4). Every dispatch these branches make for a builder role (coder, tester, uiux) is a builder dispatch, and the ladder applies to it unchanged, naming `checkModelTierRung` and `checkOperatorRung`. No sentence tells the wave-runner to return a file to an agent outside branches 2, 3 and 4. queue-and-gate.md section 5 documents `input`, states the five branches and the precedence, and names branch 4's bound as a playbook rule the log evidences by structure and no verb enforces. test/handbackPreflight.test.ts pins every branch: each `PaperworkReason` in exactly its branch, from a map the compiler ties to the type (`satisfies Record<PaperworkReason, ...>`); each named `input` in exactly its branch, and the default for an unnamed one; the precedence (intake first, branch 3 only with no intake problem showing); the tie-break; branch 4's fields, its `causal_parent` link, its bound of one and the ladder sentence; and that the old sentence ('bounces the problem to the worker whose file it names, and does not call `gate run`') is gone, replacing the one assertion that pinned it. wave.md keeps steps 2 to 10, and the diff changes no line of step 9.

Findings f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-f945754b, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-1ecb562b, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-ca1f180a and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-246f97c8, the premises in code: every `intake` problem `bs results check` prints carries `input`, naming where it came from (a flag's file or value, the task id and artifacts dir, or a step inside the verb); the verb's `judges` label is split into `judge-dispatch`, `judge-artifact` and `judge-internal` by the rule in the objective; no other problem and no top-level key changes. test/cliResultsCheck.test.ts pins, through the built CLI, the label the code prints for each fixture: `result` for an unreadable result and for one that sets an owned field (`--as gate` and `--as coder`); `grader` for an unreadable grader file under `--as grader`; `evidence` for an `--evidence` file that is not a list (it fails in `mintFromEvidence`, before any judge close); `judge-artifact` for a handed-in grader file that is fresh but neither a list nor a grader document (`judges.artifact-not-a-list`) and for a stale one (`judges.artifact-stale`), each with a recorded grader dispatch; `judge-dispatch` for `--no-findings reviewer` with no reviewer dispatch (`judges.not-dispatched`); and `checks` for an unreadable checks file. `judge-internal` and `paperwork` need a fault inside the verb; the test reaches them if it can without editing a file outside the claims, and `notes` says whether it did. The mixed case: for the handed-in grader file that is fresh but neither a list nor a grader document, the `--as gate` preflight prints the intake problem (`input` `judge-artifact`, `judges.artifact-not-a-list`) before the stage problem `grader-invalid`, and its top-level `reason` is the intake one; `gate run` on the same line prints an `error` document and the log holds no `gate-outcome` for the task, which is why that result takes branch 2 and never goes to `gate run`. For one branch-3 defect from test/helpers/paperworkFixtures.ts (a declared artifact never written), the `--as gate` preflight and `gate run` on the same line block with the same reason, the gate runs no check command (the line's checks file holds a command that would leave a marker file, and none exists afterwards), and `readFailedRounds` over the session log holds the task's blocked round with that reason. For each `result` fixture above, `gate run` on the same line prints an `error` document and the log holds no `gate-outcome` for the task, so `readFailedRounds` counts nothing. escalation.ts, gate.ts and judges.ts do not change.

Finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-7d2d0eff: queue-and-gate.md 'An env-failure block' names the `environment` array on the `testgate-result` payload as every check's evidence, one entry per check in result order, and lists its fields there. It says that `error_class: execution.env-failure` and `environment_evidence` on the `testgate-result` and `gate-outcome` events, and `error_class` with `environmentEvidence` on the outcome `gate run` prints, appear only when a failed check's own clock gap shows sleep and hold only those checks' entries. It no longer says `environment_evidence` holds one entry per check. test/handbackPreflight.test.ts pins each point, and checks that the doc names every `CheckEnvironment` field from a list tied to the type, either an object literal that `satisfies Record<keyof CheckEnvironment, true>` or the keys of a real entry, never a free-hand list. The section's existing assertions hold.

Finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-acc5dbee: CHANGELOG.md `## Unreleased` no longer says '`gate.ts` is untouched.', 'No production change.' or 'Nothing in the npm package changes.'. The task-6 bullet says what the release does (the gate writes the events it wrote before; recurrence reads the class when it counts), and the task-5 bullet and the CLI-tests entry each say what their own change touches. The epic's `### Added` list has an entry for `task-7-close-review-fixes`. test/handbackPreflight.test.ts pins the three absences in the Unreleased text up to its first `### Fixed` heading, and adds `task-7-close-review-fixes` to the task ids it requires.

Every `bs ...` invocation in the changed files parses against usage.ts (test/docCommands.test.ts passes); `node scripts/sync-shared-fragments.mjs --check` reports no drift and no unused fragment; `git diff --name-only <base>...HEAD` lists only this task's claims, so no other worker template, no fragment, no SHARED region, .claude/skills/bs/dispatch.md, escalation.ts, gate.ts, testgate.ts, paperwork.ts, file under test/helpers/ or budgets.yml changes; `notes` quotes that list and maps each of the twelve finding ids (the four closing ones and the eight pre-code ones) to the criteria and tests that answer it.

Diff check (AC8), run by the coder before hand-back and re-run by the grader: `git diff <base>...HEAD -U0 | /usr/bin/grep -E '^\+[^+].*(\.(skip|only|todo|fails)\(|retry|quarantin|flaky|testTimeout|hookTimeout|timeout_ms|DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS|waitForLines)'`. `notes` carries its full output and, for every hit, why it is not a skip, retry, quarantine or larger timeout (a moved line whose value is unchanged, or prose that forbids the thing). An unexplained hit fails this criterion.

functional_clauses: `--as grader` accepts `--artifacts-dir` and refuses every other flag it refuses today; no other mode's accepted flags change; the output keeps its top-level keys and exit codes, only `intake` problems gain `input`, and the old `judges` label becomes `judge-dispatch`, `judge-artifact` or `judge-internal`; the preflight stays read-only and runs no check command.

Every return of a file to an agent is a counted `gate run` round (branch 3), a judge turn under the existing judge rules (branch 2), or a logged return of a worker's result bounded at one per task (branch 4); a problem in the verb or the log goes to the epic session (branch 5), never to an agent. Every builder dispatch these branches make obeys the ladder unchanged. Nothing changes escalation.ts, its counting, budgets.yml's `escalation_ladder`, gate.ts, judges.ts or any gate stage.
No text tells an agent to drop a flag, change a verdict, a finding or a test, or skip a gate run to get a clean preflight; the grader keeps `--artifacts-dir` on its line.

Only the claimed files change. The one existing assertion that changes is the step-7 assertion in test/handbackPreflight.test.ts that pins the sentence finding 5f8da50c removes (`while it exits 1 ... does not call gate run`); it is replaced by the stricter assertions of criterion 5. Every other existing assertion holds unchanged.
Each acceptance criterion names the finding it answers, and each is pinned by a test this task adds or changes.
nonfunctional_clauses: Read factory/specs/active/bs-gate-bounce/epic-spec.md before starting. Do not edit it: it sits outside every task's claims. Put one Progress line for it in the result `notes` (what changed, and anything a later task must know); the epic session copies it in at merge.
TDD: write each new test first, run it and watch it fail for the stated reason, then implement until it passes.

Before hand-back run, in full: `pnpm run build`, root `pnpm run test` (the whole suite, never a scoped file), `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run typecheck:test` and `pnpm exec biome check .` (the whole repo, never a scoped path); report each exit code and the tail of each output. `pnpm run build` comes first: the new tests run the built CLI. `pnpm run test` is a full suite, so it runs exactly as your template's heavy-run section says (`bs heavy run`): make a fresh output file with `mktemp` where that section puts it (under `<work-root>/state/results/`), start `bs heavy run --label <task-id>-coder -- pnpm run test` into it in the background (Bash `run_in_background: true`), then wait in the foreground with `bs heavy wait --file <out>`, calling it again while it reports `"done": false`; never one blocking foreground call, which outlasts the Bash tool timeout. Build, typecheck, typecheck:test and biome are not heavy (wave.md step 7, "Heavy checks") and run directly in the foreground.

Also run `bash scripts/check.sh` in full and read the tail of its output, not only its exit code; name every step it printed as SKIP. It runs the full coverage suites and e2e, so it is heavy too: start `bs heavy run --label <task-id>-coder -- bash scripts/check.sh` in the background into a fresh `mktemp` output file and wait with `bs heavy wait --file <out>`, as above.

A test that takes a lock points it at a temporary directory, never the machine's: test/setup.ts already sets BS_HEAVY_LOCK_DIR to a per-file `mkdtemp` directory, and a test that passes its own lock directory makes it with `mkdtemp` and removes it afterwards. A test that runs `gate run` or `bs results check` points `BS_HOME` or `--state-dir` at a `mkdtemp` directory, never the machine's state.

Weaken nothing: add no `.skip`, `.only`, `.todo`, `.fails`, `retry`, quarantine list or flaky marker; raise no `testTimeout`, `hookTimeout`, `timeout_ms`, `waitForLines` default, `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` or any other timeout or deadline; remove, loosen or reorder no existing assertion, gate stage, grader, judge, review round or verifier.

No other project's name, no client code and no absolute home-directory path (`/Users/...`, `/home/...`) in any committed file, test fixture included; fixtures use placeholder paths. Say "dogfood epics" for the factory's own client runs.
Add no runtime or dev dependency.
Do not edit anything under factory/policies/.

Priorities, in order: quality first, speed second, tokens third. Nothing in this task removes, skips or makes conditional a judge, a review round, a verifier pass or a gate check, and no role's model tier is lowered. Stay inside this task's claims.
Line numbers in this spec are at integration head 6365aca3 (`bs/bs-gate-bounce/integration`); the symbol named beside each one is the reference if a line has moved.
Write operator-facing prose in English, plain and short; keep each file's existing structure and headings.
No fragment or SHARED region is edited in this task; run `node scripts/sync-shared-fragments.mjs --check` and report its output.
The doc tests read a backticked dotted token in an instruction file as an error code: in wave.md and queue-and-gate.md backtick only codes that exist, and check them by running the doc tests.

Templates stay stack-neutral outside the SHARED regions: the one bs-grader.md sentence names no tool, package manager or test runner, and the agent-template neutrality step of `bash scripts/check.sh` passes.
